blocks.text: Quick verdict

Proxy-Cheap is the cheaper choice and the right one for country-level scraping on easier targets, where its promotional $0.78/GB rate is very hard to beat. ProxyEmpire is the better choice when you need city or ISP targeting, sticky sessions for account work, or more confidence in success rates: independent testers ranked its pool among the largest they measured in 2026. If budget is tight, start with Proxy-Cheap; if a failed request costs you more than the bandwidth, start with ProxyEmpire.

ProxyEmpire and Proxy-Cheap both sell residential, mobile and static proxies from one account and both appeal to cost-conscious buyers. Proxy-Cheap currently leads on headline price with rotating residential traffic advertised at $0.78/GB. ProxyEmpire costs more per gigabyte at entry but adds city and ISP targeting, 24-hour sticky sessions, bandwidth that never expires and a stronger independent testing record. This comparison weighs cheap traffic against the features that decide whether that traffic actually works on your targets.

blocks.text: ProxyEmpire in 2026: what you get

ProxyEmpire is a Bulgarian-registered provider (SWIFT SAAS LTD) that has been selling since 2020. Its residential and mobile networks share one system with 30M+ advertised IPs in 170+ countries, and country, region, city and ISP targeting are included at no extra cost. The standout policy is bandwidth rollover: prepaid traffic carries forward indefinitely, even after a subscription lapses. Proxyway's 2026 market tests found ProxyEmpire's pool was the third largest among the providers it tested.

Strengths: Prepaid traffic rolls over indefinitely; ISP/ASN targeting included at no extra cost; Cheap $1.97 trial covering residential and mobile; Unlimited residential option priced per day. Weak spots: Smaller advertised pool than the big three; Exact GB thresholds for each tier only shown at checkout; Weaker results on Google in some independent tests.
Proxy-Cheap in 2026: what you get

Proxy-Cheap has sold proxies since 2018 and says it serves 45,000+ customers. It offers seven product types: static residential (ISP) in IPv4 and IPv6, rotating residential, datacenter IPv4 and IPv6, and static and rotating mobile. Rotating residential is pure pay-as-you-go with no monthly plan, and the site claims coverage in 180+ countries. Targeting is mainly country and ISP level, and all products support SOCKS5 including UDP. It is a strong value pick, though independent benchmarks of its rotating pool have been mixed.

Strengths: Very low per-GB price while the promotion runs; No monthly commitment on rotating residential; Broad catalog including IPv6 and static mobile; SOCKS5 with UDP support. Weak spots: Targeting is mostly country and ISP, not city; Residential pool size not separately published; Mixed results in some independent benchmarks.
Pricing: ProxyEmpire vs Proxy-Cheap

ProxyEmpire's rotating residential pricing currently starts at $3.50/GB (shown as 50% off a $7 list price) and steps down through several tiers to $1.50/GB at 1 TB, with custom pricing from about $0.75/GB above 5 TB. Rotating mobile starts at $4.50/GB, rotating datacenter at about $0.65/GB, and a flat-rate unlimited residential plan is sold by the day.

Proxy-Cheap's rotating residential proxies are pay-as-you-go, currently listed from $0.78/GB (a promotional price against a $2.60/GB list rate). Static residential ISP proxies start around $2.44 per IP per month, datacenter IPv4 at about $1.49, datacenter IPv6 from $0.15, and rotating mobile at $5.99/GB.

Buying 10 GB, you would pay about $7.80 with Proxy-Cheap and $35 with ProxyEmpire: a 78% saving in Proxy-Cheap's favour. At 100 GB, a like-for-like total is harder to state because ProxyEmpire does not publish an exact price for that volume; Proxy-Cheap comes to about $78. The sticker price is only half of it. ProxyEmpire's unused traffic carries forward, while Proxy-Cheap's does not (pay-as-you-go balance, no monthly commitment), so if your usage swings from month to month ProxyEmpire can work out cheaper than the per-GB numbers suggest.
Pool size, coverage and targeting

Proxy-Cheap does not publish a clear residential pool figure, so a size comparison is not possible on published data. ProxyEmpire lists '30M+' and Proxy-Cheap lists 'Not separately published (155M+ claimed across all products)'. In practice, what matters is how many unique IPs you get in the countries you target, which you can measure in a short trial by sending a few thousand requests and counting distinct exit addresses. For coverage, ProxyEmpire lists 170+ countries and Proxy-Cheap lists 180+. On targeting, ProxyEmpire offers country, region, city and ISP/ASN (included by default), while Proxy-Cheap offers country and ISP.
Protocols, sessions and setup

Both providers support SOCKS5 as well as HTTP(S), so either will plug into scrapers, anti-detect browsers and automation tools that expect a SOCKS endpoint. On sessions, ProxyEmpire offers rotating or sticky sessions up to 24 hours, and Proxy-Cheap offers rotating and sticky sessions. Both use a backconnect gateway: you point your tool at one host and port, and choose country, city or session behaviour through parameters in the username.
Which is better for your use case?

General web scraping: ProxyEmpire. ProxyEmpire has the edge here. Why: stable connections and traffic that never expires. How Proxy-Cheap compares: cheap traffic, though independent benchmark results have been mixed.

SERP and rank tracking: close call. Both are reasonable choices here. ProxyEmpire: Google was its weakest target in independent tests. Proxy-Cheap: workable for light rank tracking at a low cost. Let price and the countries you need decide.

Social media and multi-account management: tie. Neither has a clear edge. With ProxyEmpire: residential and mobile IPs with 24-hour sticky sessions. With Proxy-Cheap: cheap static ISP and mobile IPs for persistent identities. Run the same small test on both before committing.
E-commerce price and stock monitoring: ProxyEmpire wins. The deciding factor for ProxyEmpire: free city and ISP targeting. The limitation on the Proxy-Cheap side: fine for country-level price checks.
Ad verification and geo-testing: ProxyEmpire. ProxyEmpire has the edge here. Why: ISP-level targeting at no extra cost. How Proxy-Cheap compares: lacks city-level targeting on rotating residential.
Tight budgets: Proxy-Cheap. Proxy-Cheap has the edge here. Why: the lowest advertised per-GB price in this pairing. How ProxyEmpire compares: rollover means nothing you pay for is wasted.
Trials, verification and billing fine print

Before you pay, check how each provider lets you test. ProxyEmpire: $1.97 trial with 100 MB residential and 50 MB mobile. Proxy-Cheap: 7-day $1.99 trial on static residential and datacenter IPs. Verification and payment rules differ too. ProxyEmpire: Standard verification. Proxy-Cheap: Light; card, PayPal, Alipay and crypto accepted. Whichever you choose, measure cost per successful request rather than cost per gigabyte: retries, blocked pages and heavy page assets all burn bandwidth, and a cheaper network that fails more often can end up costing more. Blocking images and fonts in your scraper, reusing sessions where a target allows it, and capping concurrency are the quickest ways to cut the bill on either provider.
How to test ProxyEmpire and Proxy-Cheap before you commit
The quickest way to choose between ProxyEmpire and Proxy-Cheap is a side-by-side test on the sites and countries you actually care about:

1. Buy the smallest option on each side (ProxyEmpire: $1.97 trial with 100 MB residential and 50 MB mobile; Proxy-Cheap: 7-day $1.99 trial on static residential and datacenter IPs). 2. Pick three to five real target URLs and the two or three countries that matter most, and send the same number of requests (a few hundred is enough) through each provider at the same time of day.
3. Record success rate, median response time, CAPTCHAs or blocks, and the number of unique exit IPs you received per country.
4. Divide what you spent by the number of successful, correctly located responses to get cost per useful request, then scale that to your monthly volume.
Bottom line

Across the six use cases above, ProxyEmpire comes out ahead in 3, Proxy-Cheap in 1, and 2 are ties. That makes ProxyEmpire the safer default if you are unsure, but the right answer still depends on your volume and targets: ProxyEmpire is strongest for teams that hate losing unused bandwidth, while Proxy-Cheap is strongest for price-sensitive scraping at moderate difficulty. If you can, spend a few dollars testing both on the exact sites and countries you care about; a one-hour test tells you more than any spec sheet.
